hints: The product can be 3, 4, 5 or 6. No digit can be 0.
List the digit groups for each product, like {1, 1, 3} for 3, then count the ways to arrange each group.
1.why:
Product 3: {1,1,3}, 3 ways. Product 4: {1,1,4} and {1,2,2}, 3 + 3 ways. Product 5: {1,1,5}, 3 ways. Product 6: {1,1,6} 3 ways and {1,2,3} 6 ways.

Total 3 + 6 + 3 + 9 = 21.

hints: f(5 + x) = f(5 − x) means the graph is a mirror image about x = 5.
If r is a root, what other number must also be a root?
2.why: The graph is symmetric about x = 5, so roots come in pairs 5 + a and 5 − a, each pair adding to 10. Four roots make two pairs: 20. (40 counts each root as 10; 10 counts only one pair.)

hints: Write each balance after t years from Veeru's start. Joy has only t − 2 years of interest.
At one-third speed the trip takes 3 times as long. Use the 30-minute delay to find the usual trip time.
On the way back, 9 minutes are gone after covering only 5 minutes' worth of distance. How much time is left for the rest?
4.why:
3T − T = 30, so the usual trip T is 15 minutes. Going back, 5 minutes at usual speed covers a third of the way, then 4 minutes are lost. 6 minutes remain for the other two-thirds, which normally takes 10 minutes.

Speed must rise to 10/6 of usual: about 67% more, so 67.

hints: Write every log in terms of natural logs (or any one base).
log<sub>6</sub> √5 = ½ log<sub>6</sub> 5. The ln 5 on both sides cancels.
5.why: ln5/ln4 = (ln y/ln4) × (½ ln5/ln6). Cancel ln5 and ln4: 1 = ln y ÷ (2 ln6), so ln y = 2 ln6 and y = 36.

hints: What's the smallest value 2<sup>x</sup> + 2<sup>−x</sup> can take, and for which x?
What's the largest value the right side can take, and for which x?
6.why: The left side is at least 2 (equal only at x = 0). The right side is at most 2 (equal only at x = 2). Both would have to equal 2 at the same x, which can't happen. 0 solutions.

hints: Each car covers, after the meeting, the distance the other covered before it.
This gives (v1/v2)² = t2/t1, using the times after the meeting.
Double both conditions to clear the fractions.
Subtract one from the other to get B − A. Then remember all three are positive integers.
8.why: 2A + B + C = 10 and A + 2B + C = 14. Subtracting: B − A = 4. With A = 1, B = 5, C = 3 works. A = 2 gives B = 6 and C = 0, which isn't positive. So A + B = 6.

hints: 4096 = 2<sup>12</sup> and 64 = 2<sup>6</sup>. What power of x gives 64?
aabb = 1100a + 11b. What values can a and b take?
Even means b is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Every a pairs with every b, so average them separately.
10.why: a runs 1 to 9 (average 5), b runs over 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 (average 4). Mean = 1100 × 5 + 11 × 4 = 5544.

hints: Let t = x + 1/x and solve the quadratic in t.
For real x, x + 1/x can't be between −2 and 2.
11.why: t² − 3t + 2 = 0 gives t = 1 or 2. t = 1 has no real x. t = 2 gives only x = 1. So 1 root.

hints: Let the desktop cost D, so the laptop costs 50000 − D.
Overall profit is 2% of 50000 = 1000.
Spread the 100 students as evenly as you can over 12 months.
100 ÷ 12 is a little over 8.
13.why: If every month had 8 or fewer, there'd be at most 96 students. So some month has at least 9, and 9 is reachable (four months of 9, eight of 8). Answer 9.

hints: The train's length = (train speed − walker speed) × crossing time, for each walker.
Set the two lengths equal to find the train's speed.
14.why: (v − 2) × 90 = (v − 4) × 100, so v = 22 km/h. The length is 20 km/h × 90 s. Crossing a post takes 20 × 90 ÷ 22 ≈ 81.8 s, nearest 82.

hints: A power equals 1 in three ways: base 1, exponent 0 (with a non-zero base), or base −1 with an even exponent.
Check each case for positive integers x.
15.why: Base 1: x² − 7x + 10 = 0, x = 2 or 5. Exponent 0: x = 6 or 7 (base is 5 or 11, not 0). Base −1: x = 3 or 4, with exponents 12 and 6, both even. Total 6. (Missing the base −1 case gives 4.)

hints: Rewrite |x| − y ≤ 1 as y ≥ |x| − 1. Sketch this V shape.
Cut it between y = 0 and y = 1. What shape is left?
16.why: At y = 0, x runs from −1 to 1 (width 2). At y = 1, x runs from −2 to 2 (width 4). It's a trapezium of height 1: (2 + 4)/2 × 1 = 3.

hints: The small top cone has height 27 − 18 = 9, a third of the full height.
Volumes of similar cones scale with the cube of the height.
17.why: Top cone = V/27, bottom piece = 26V/27. The difference is 25V/27 = 225, so V = 243.

hints: Find the rhombus's side and area from its diagonals.
For a shape with an inscribed circle, area = ½ × perimeter × radius.
The two speeds differ by 35 minutes of travel time. Use that to find the distance.
Then he has 50 minutes for that distance.
19.why: d/8 − d/15 = 35/60, so 7d/120 = 7/12 and d = 10 km. 10 km in 50 minutes is 12 km/h.

hints: b must divide both 432 and 96. What's their HCF?
c = 96/b must be below 9, so b must be at least 11. Try each possible b.
20.why: b divides 48 and b > 10.67, so b is 12, 16, 24 or 48. a + b + c = 528/b + b gives 56, 49, 46, 59. The smallest is 46 (a = 18, b = 24, c = 4).

hints: Take log base 2 of both sides.
log<sub>3</sub> 5 = log<sub>2</sub> 5 ÷ log<sub>2</sub> 3.
21.why: y² log3 5 = log2 3 × log2 5. Replace log3 5 and cancel log2 5: y² = (log2 3)². y is negative, so y = −log2 3 = log2(1/3). (Option C is the positive root.)

hints: The circle's diameter equals the shorter side. Unpainted = ⅔ painted means the sheet is 5/3 of the circle's area.
Find r from 5/3 × πr² = 135, then the other side from the area.
22.why: πr² × 5/3 = 135, so r² = 81/π and the short side is 2r = 18/√π. The long side = 135 ÷ (18/√π) = 7.5√π. Perimeter = 15√π + 36/√π = 3√π(5 + 12/π).

hints: Take 100 people and fill a 2 × 2 table: young/old by literate/illiterate.
Young literates are 25% of the 65 literates.
23.why: Literates 65: young 16.25, old 48.75. Illiterates 35: young 28 − 16.25 = 11.75, old 23.25. 23.25 ÷ 35 ≈ 66.4%, nearest 66.

hints: Weight = volume × weight per unit volume, for each metal.
Multiply 3 : 4 : 7 by 5 : 2 : 6 term by term.
Work backwards from the last child.
Before a child, the stock was (stock after + 1) × 2.
Track dye and water separately: start with 16 dye, 24 water.
Dye doesn't change when water is added. Find the water at 2 : 5, then take out a quarter of each.
26.why: At 2 : 5, water = 40 (dye 16). Taking out a quarter leaves dye 12, water 30. For 2 : 3 with 30 water, dye must be 20: add 8 litres.
